text.p: Pete Sampras advanced to the semifinals of the $4.45 million Lipton Championships on Wednesday in a walkover after a freak accident befell his quarterfinal round opponent.
Hendrik Dreekman of Germany sprained an ankle walking back to his hotel in downtown Miami on Tuesday evening and was forced to withdraw from the quarterfinal match.

The day's real drama was reserved for the women's quarterfinal between third-seeded Jana Novotna of the Czech Republic and 8th-seeded Iva Majoli of Croatia. Novotna eventually won the two hour and 24-minute cliff-hanger 6-3 2-6 7-6 (9-7.)
Novotna, ranked 4 and Majoli, ranked 10, battled evenly in the first two sets.
Novotna attacked the net, and Majoli used her fierce groundstrokes and passing shots, with Novotna winning the first set 6-2 and the Croatian the second 6-3.

Both players came out flat at the start of the third set. The players exchanged three service breaks before Novotna held for a 3-1 lead. But the woman best remembered for choking away the Wimbledon final in 1993, twice failed to serve out the match at 5-4 and 6-5.
Instead, the set went to a tiebreaker.

Novotna missed her first match point at 6-5, slicing an approach shot wide. At 7-6, she faltered again with a wild forehand error. Instead, it was Majoli, steady throughout the match, who gave away the third match point with a smash wide.
Novotna dropped to the ground in relief and disbelief and the two women hugged before leaving the court.

"When she missed that overhead it was such a relief," said Novotna, playing her first tournament since recovering from a bout with shingles. "I was lying there saying, 'that's it. I don't have to run any further.' Because of the shingles I wasn't expecting very much from this tournament, and here I am."
Majoli said her poor serving cost her.
"When your serve isn't working you are rushing and making mistakes," she said. "I made a lot of errors."
Majoli had 52 unforced errors in the match but Novotna was worse with 63.
Dreekman's withdrawal followed a curious tournament tradition of players suffering strange accidents and injuries at The Lipton.

The most notorious occurred in 1989 when Thomas Muster of Austria was hit by a car outside his hotel in Miami, the night before his final with Ivan Lendl. The injury took Muster off the tour for six months.
Last year, Goran Ivanisevic defaulted in the final with Andre Agassi after three games, suffering from a stiff neck, a problem he had sustained during the night.
In 1994, Sampras had delayed the start of the final for two hours with stomach problems, before defeating Agassi for the title.

Boris Becker claimed food poisoning from fish before withdrawing from the event in 1989. In 1993, Becker advanced to the third round without playing a match when second-round opponent, Gianluca Pozzi, was rushed to the hospital with appendicitis. Becker withdrew with the flu one round later.
Dreekman said he had hoped to recover in time to play. "I was still hoping I might be able to play today," he said. "But this morning I couldn't move my feet, nothing. It was impossible."
